readings.title: Elohim, the Singular Judge
readings.subtitle: Thanksgiving for the Appointed Time of Justice
readings.text: [Psalm 75:1] We shall give thanks to <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, we shall give thanks! And <dn>Your</dn> Name is near! <dn>Your</dn> wonders shall be declared! [2] <dq>When <dn>I</dn> seize <dn>את</dn> the appointed time, It is <dn>I</dn> who judge in uprightness.</dq> [3] <dq>The earth and all its inhabitants are melted; It is <dn>I</dn> who set <dn>את</dn> its columns firm. Selah.</dq>

readings.title: The Futility of Arrogance
readings.subtitle: Exaltation Proceeds Only from the Universal Authority
readings.text: [Psalm 75:4] <dq><dn>I</dn> said to the boasters, ‘Do not boast,’ And to the wrong, ‘Do not lift up the horn.</dq> [5] <dq>Do not lift up your horn on high (<dn>You</dn> speak with a stiff neck).’ ”</dq> [6] For exaltations are neither from the east, Nor from the west nor from the wilderness. [7] But <dn>Elohim</dn> is the Judge – <dn>He</dn> puts down one, And exalts another.

readings.title: The Cup of Divine Righteousness
readings.subtitle: Severing the Authority of the Wrong
readings.text: [Psalm 75:8] For a cup is in the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, And the wine shall foam; It is filled with a mixture, And <dn>He</dn> pours it out. All the wrong of the earth drink, Draining it to the dregs. [9] But <dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> declare forever, <dn>I</dn> sing praises to the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya‛aqoḇ. [10] <dq>“And <dn>את</dn> all the horns of the wrong <dn>I</dn> cut off; <dn>את</dn> The horns of the righteous are lifted up.”</dq>

readings.title: The Victorious Elohim of Tsiyon
readings.subtitle: Shattering the Instruments of War
readings.text: [Psalm 76:1] In Yehuḏah <dn>Elohim</dn> is known; <dn>His</dn> Name is great in Yisra’ĕl. [2] And <dn>His</dn> booth is in Shalĕm, And <dn>His</dn> dwelling place in Tsiyon. [3] There <dn>He</dn> broke <dn>את</dn> the arrows of the bow, <dn>את</dn> The shield and <dn>את</dn> the sword and <dn>את</dn> the battle-axe. Selah.

readings.title: The Resplendent Rebuke
readings.subtitle: Stripping the Strength of the Stout-Hearted
readings.text: [Psalm 76:4] <dn>You</dn> are resplendent, More excellent than mountains of prey. [5] The stout-hearted have been stripped; They slept their sleep; And none of the mighty men have found their hands. [6] At <dn>Your</dn> rebuke, O <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya‛aqoḇ, Both the rider and horse lay stunned.

readings.title: The Absolute Authority of the Righteous Judge
readings.subtitle: Right-Ruling to Save the Meek
readings.text: [Psalm 76:7] <dn>You</dn>, <dn>You</dn> are to be feared; And who would stand in <dn>Your</dn> presence When <dn>You</dn> are displeased? [8] From heaven <dn>You</dn> shall cause judgment to be heard; The earth shall fear, and shall be still, [9] When <dn>Elohim</dn> arises to right-ruling, To save all the meek of the earth. Selah.

readings.title: The Wrath of Mankind Harnessed
readings.subtitle: Severing the Spirit of Earthly Sovereigns
readings.text: [Psalm 76:10] For the wrath of mankind praises <dn>You</dn>, With the remainder of wrath <dn>You</dn> gird <dn>Yourself</dn>! [11] Make vows to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and pay them. Let all who are around <dn>Him</dn> bring presents To the One to be feared. [12] <dn>He</dn> cuts off the spirit of leaders, <dn>He</dn> is awesome to the sovereigns of the earth!

readings.title: The Night of Distress
readings.subtitle: A Diligent Search of the Spirit
readings.text: [Psalm 77:1] My voice is to <dn>Elohim</dn>, and I cry; My voice is to <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> listened to me. [2] In the day of my distress I sought <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>; My hand was stretched out in the night And it did not cease, My being refused to be comforted. [3] I remembered <dn>Elohim</dn>, and groaned; I complained, and my spirit grew faint. Selah. [4] <dn>You</dn> ceased the watches of my eyes, I was too troubled to speak. [5] I have thought about the days of old, The years long past. [6] I remember my song in the night, I meditate within my heart, And my spirit searches diligently.

readings.title: Wrestling with the Covenant Promise
readings.subtitle: Meditating on the Deeds of Yah
readings.text: [Psalm 77:7] Would <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> reject forever, And never again be pleased? [8] Has <dn>His</dn> loving-commitment ceased forever, Has the promise failed for all generations? [9] Has <dn>Ĕl</dn> forgotten to show favour? Has <dn>He</dn> shut up <dn>His</dn> compassions in displeasure? Selah. [10] And I said, “This is my grief: That the right hand of the Most High has changed.” [11] I remember the deeds of <dn>Yah</dn>, For I remember <dn>Your</dn> wonders of old. [12] And I shall meditate on all <dn>Your</dn> work, And talk of <dn>Your</dn> deeds.

readings.title: The Set-Apart Architecture of El
readings.subtitle: Redemption by the Right Arm
readings.text: [Psalm 77:13] <dn>Your</dn> way, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, is in Set-apartness; Who is a great <dn>Ĕl</dn> like <dn>Elohim</dn>? [14] <dn>You</dn> are the <dn>Ĕl</dn> who does wonders; <dn>You</dn> have made known <dn>Your</dn> strength among the peoples. [15] By <dn>Your</dn> arm <dn>You</dn> have redeemed <dn>Your</dn> people, The sons of Ya‛aqoḇ and Yosĕph. Selah.

readings.title: The Cosmos Trembles at His Voice
readings.subtitle: Leading the Flock Through Great Waters
readings.text: [Psalm 77:16] The waters saw <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>Elohim</dn>; The waters saw <dn>You</dn>, they were afraid; The depths also trembled. [17] The clouds poured out water; The heavens rumbled; Also, <dn>Your</dn> arrows flashed back and forth. [18] The voice of <dn>Your</dn> thunder rolled along; Lightnings lit up the world; The earth trembled and shook. [19] <dn>Your</dn> way was in the sea, And <dn>Your</dn> path in the great waters, And <dn>Your</dn> footsteps were not known. [20] <dn>You</dn> did lead <dn>Your</dn> people like a flock By the hand of Mosheh and Aharon.

readings.title: The Generational Mandate
readings.subtitle: Transmitting the Praises and the Torah
readings.text: [Psalm 78:1] My people, give ear to my Torah, Incline your ears to the words of my mouth. [2] I open my mouth in a parable; I utter riddles of old, [3] Which we have heard and known, For our fathers have related them to us. [4] We do not hide them from their children, Relating to the generation to come the praises of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, And <dn>His</dn> strength and <dn>His</dn> wonders which <dn>He</dn> has done. [5] For <dn>He</dn> raised <dn>את</dn> a witness in Ya‛aqoḇ, And set <dn>את</dn> a Torah in Yisra’ĕl, Which <dn>He</dn> commanded our fathers, To teach them to their children; [6] That it might be known to a generation to come, To children who would be born, To rise up and relate them to their children, [7] And place their trust in <dn>Elohim</dn>, And not forget the works of <dn>Ĕl</dn>, But watch over <dn>His</dn> commands, [8] And not be like their fathers, A stubborn and rebellious generation, A generation which did not prepare its heart, Whose spirit was not steadfast to <dn>Ĕl</dn>.

readings.title: The Retreat of Ephrayim
readings.subtitle: Forgetting the Wonders of Tso‛an
readings.text: [Psalm 78:9] The children of Ephrayim, armed bowmen, Turned back in the day of battle. [10] They did not guard <dn>את</dn> the covenant of <dn>Elohim</dn>, And they refused to walk in <dn>His</dn> Torah, [11] And they forgot <dn>His</dn> deeds And <dn>His</dn> wonders which <dn>He</dn> had shown them. [12] <dn>He</dn> did wonders in the sight of their fathers, In the land of Mitsrayim, in the field of Tso‛an. [13] <dn>He</dn> split <dn>את</dn> the sea and caused them to pass through, And <dn>He</dn> made the waters stand up like a heap, [14] And led them with the cloud by day, And all the night with a light of fire. [15] <dn>He</dn> split <dn>את</dn> the rocks in the wilderness, And made them drink, as from the great depths, [16] And brought forth streams from the rock, And caused waters to come down as rivers.

readings.title: Severing Trust in the Wilderness
readings.subtitle: A Failure to Lean on His Deliverance
readings.text: [Psalm 78:17] Yet they sinned still more against <dn>Him</dn> To rebel against the Most High in the desert. [18] And they tried <dn>Ĕl</dn> in their heart By asking food according to their desire. [19] And they spoke against <dn>Elohim</dn>. They said, “Is <dn>Ĕl</dn> able to set a table in the wilderness? [20] “Look, <dn>He</dn> struck the rock, So that the waters gushed out, And the streams overflowed. Is <dn>He</dn> able to give bread also? Would <dn>He</dn> provide meat for <dn>His</dn> people?” [21] Therefore <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> heard, and <dn>He</dn> was wroth; So a fire was kindled against Ya‛aqoḇ, And displeasure also came up against Yisra’ĕl, [22] Because they did not believe in <dn>Elohim</dn>, Neither did they trust in <dn>His</dn> deliverance.

readings.title: Opening the Doors of the Heavens
readings.subtitle: The Fatal Cost of Unrestrained Desire
readings.text: [Psalm 78:23] Yet <dn>He</dn> had commanded the clouds above, And opened the doors of the heavens, [24] And <dn>He</dn> rained down manna on them to eat, And <dn>He</dn> gave them the grain of the heavens. [25] Men ate bread of the mighty; <dn>He</dn> sent them provisions to satisfaction. [26] <dn>He</dn> made an east wind blow in the heavens; And by <dn>His</dn> power <dn>He</dn> brought in the south wind. [27] And <dn>He</dn> rained meat on them like the dust, And winged birds like the sand of the seas, [28] And let them fall in the midst of <dn>His</dn> camp, All around <dn>His</dn> Dwelling Place. [29] So they ate and were completely satisfied, For <dn>He</dn> brought them what they desired. [30] They had not turned away from their desire, Their food was still in their mouths, [31] When the wrath of <dn>Elohim</dn> came against them, And <dn>He</dn> killed among their fat ones, And <dn>He</dn> struck down the choice ones of Yisra’ĕl.

readings.title: Flattery from a Crooked Heart
readings.subtitle: The Compassionate Restraint of His Wrath
readings.text: [Psalm 78:32] In spite of all this they still sinned, And did not believe in <dn>His</dn> wonders. [33] So <dn>He</dn> ended their days in a breath, And their years in trouble. [34] When <dn>He</dn> killed them, then they sought <dn>Him</dn>, And they returned and did earnestly seek <dn>Ĕl</dn>. [35] And they remembered that <dn>Elohim</dn> was their rock, And the Most High <dn>Ĕl</dn> their redeemer. [36] But they flattered <dn>Him</dn> with their mouth, And they lied to <dn>Him</dn> with their tongue, [37] For their heart was not steadfast with <dn>Him</dn>, And they were not true to <dn>His</dn> covenant. [38] But <dn>He</dn>, the Compassionate One, Pardoned crookedness, And did not destroy them. And many a time <dn>He</dn> turned <dn>His</dn> displeasure away, And did not stir up all <dn>His</dn> wrath. [39] For <dn>He</dn> remembered that they were but flesh, A passing breath that does not return.

readings.title: Provoking the Set-Apart One
readings.subtitle: The Decrees of Systemic Ruin in Mitsrayim
readings.text: [Psalm 78:40] How often they rebelled against <dn>Him</dn> in the wilderness, And grieved <dn>Him</dn> in the desert! [41] And again and again they tried <dn>Ĕl</dn>, And provoked <dn>את</dn> the Set-apart One of Yisra’ĕl. [42] They did not remember <dn>His</dn> hand, The day when <dn>He</dn> redeemed them from the adversary, [43] How <dn>He</dn> worked <dn>His</dn> signs in Mitsrayim, And <dn>His</dn> wonders in the field of Tso‛an. [44] <dn>He</dn> turned their rivers into blood, And they could not drink their streams. [45] <dn>He</dn> sent among them swarms of flies which devoured them, And frogs which destroyed them, [46] And gave their crops to the caterpillar, And their labour to the locust. [47] <dn>He</dn> destroyed their vines with hail, And their sycamore trees with frost, [48] And gave their beasts over to the hail, And their livestock to bolts of fire. [49] <dn>He</dn> sent on them the burning of <dn>His</dn> displeasure, Wrath, and rage, and distress, A deputation of messengers of evils. [50] <dn>He</dn> made a path for <dn>His</dn> displeasure; <dn>He</dn> did not spare their being from death, But gave their life over to the plague. [51] And <dn>He</dn> struck all the first-born in Mitsrayim, The first-fruits of strength in the tents of Ḥam,

readings.title: Allotting the Measured Inheritance
readings.subtitle: The Treachery of Carved Images
readings.text: [Psalm 78:52] Then made <dn>His</dn> own people go forth like sheep, And led them in the wilderness like a flock. [53] And <dn>He</dn> led them on safely, And they did not fear, But the sea covered their enemies. [54] And <dn>He</dn> brought them to the border of <dn>His</dn> set-apart place, <dn>את</dn> This mountain which <dn>His</dn> right hand had gained, [55] And drove out nations before them, And allotted them a measured inheritance, And made the tribes of Yisra’ĕl dwell in their tents. [56] Yet they tried and rebelled Against the Most High <dn>Elohim</dn>, And did not guard <dn>His</dn> witnesses, [57] But they turned back And acted treacherously like their fathers; They twisted like a treacherous bow. [58] For they enraged <dn>Him</dn> with their high places, And moved <dn>Him</dn> to jealousy with their carved images.

readings.title: The Departure from Shiloh
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Awakens to Repel the Adversary
readings.text: [Psalm 78:59] When <dn>Elohim</dn> heard this, <dn>He</dn> was wroth, And greatly despised Yisra’ĕl, [60] And <dn>He</dn> left <dn>את</dn> the Dwelling Place of Shiloh, The Tent which <dn>He</dn> had set up among men. [61] And <dn>He</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> strength into captivity, And <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> comeliness into the hand of the adversary. [62] And <dn>He</dn> gave <dn>His</dn> people over to the sword, And <dn>He</dn> was wroth with <dn>His</dn> inheritance. [63] <dn>His</dn> young men were consumed by fire, And <dn>His</dn> maidens were not praised. [64] <dn>His</dn> priests fell by the sword, And their widows could not weep. [65] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> awoke as one asleep, As a mighty man who shouts because of wine. [66] And <dn>He</dn> struck <dn>His</dn> adversaries backward, <dn>He</dn> put them to an everlasting reproach.

readings.title: The Election of Tsiyon
readings.subtitle: Shepherding Ya‛aqoḇ with Integrity of Heart
readings.text: [Psalm 78:67] Then <dn>He</dn> rejected <dn>את</dn> the tent of Yosĕph, And did not choose the tribe of Ephrayim, [68] But chose <dn>את</dn> the tribe of Yehuḏah, <dn>את</dn> Mount Tsiyon, which <dn>He</dn> loved. [69] And <dn>He</dn> built <dn>His</dn> set-apart place like the heights, Like the earth <dn>He</dn> founded it forever. [70] And <dn>He</dn> chose <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ <dn>His</dn> servant, And took him from the sheepfolds; [71] <dn>He</dn> brought him in from tending the ewes, To shepherd <dn>את</dn> Ya‛aqoḇ <dn>His</dn> people, And <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl <dn>His</dn> inheritance. [72] And he shepherded them According to the integrity of his heart, And led them by the skill of his hands.
